_note: Registry of the technical standards a template field or a DPP system may relate to. Keys are UNDATED designations; editions are listed per entry. A standard never makes a field required - only `regulationRef.kind: legislation` can. `ojCitation` is present only where an implementing decision published the reference in the Official Journal, which is what confers a presumption of conformity. `verified: true` means the title and status were checked against the OJ, the publisher's own catalogue (CEN/CENELEC, ISO Open Data, BSI, GS1) or the standard's own text, and `notes` names the source; `false` means `subject` is a descriptive label, not the official title. Every CEN/CENELEC member adopts an EN identically as a national standard (e.g. DIN EN, BDS EN) - those are aliases of the same text, recorded under `nationalAdoptions` where confirmed, not separate standards.

kinds.harmonised-standard: An EN whose reference is published in the OJ under an EU act; conformity gives a presumption of conformity with the provisions named.
kinds.european-standard: A published EN (or EN ISO / EN IEC) not cited in the OJ for DPP purposes.
kinds.national-standard: A standard of one national body with no EN equivalent.
kinds.industry-specification: A specification by an industry body (e.g. GS1), not a formal standard.
kinds.un-regulation: A UN Regulation annexed to the UNECE 1958 Agreement (vehicle type approval); binding where applied, not a standard.
